To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
activated variants of resolvase catalyse re combination between two copies of site 1, the binding sites for resolvase.
the synapse of the serine recombinases is formed by the sequential binding of monomers to the recombination site, and that the synapse does not form in the absence of recombination site.
the serine recombinases Tn3 resolvas and XerD assemble a synapse comprising two sites and four dimers by binding to two sites sequentially, and that the synapse can be formed without cleaving DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of recombination catalysed by the site-specific serine recombinases.
the mechanisms by which proteins bind to and modify DNA.
the molecular mechanisms that underpin the catalytic activity of a recombinase protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

activated mutants of Tn3 res are able to catalyse site I × site I reactions in vitro, and that these reactions are characterized by the formation of a stable site I × siteI × resolvase tetranucleoprotein complex.

(i) site I is a minimal binding site for resolvase; (ii) resolvase tetrams can form in vitro in the absence of res site DNA; (iii) resolvase dimmers are the minimal units that can synapse with res site DNA; and (iv) the 2– 3′ interface of resolvase subunits is essential for synapsis and cleavage of DNA
the activation mutations have altered the mechanism of recombination by the enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the activated variants have a relaxed specificity for the site I DNA sequence and are less dependent on the presence of the 2–4′ interface for catalysis, and that these changes result in a relaxed specificity for site I and a relaxed requirement for the 2–2′ interface.
the activation of resolvase by mutation is due to loss of the 2– 3′ interface between dimers.
the synapse and catalysis by resolvase are not coupled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
activated mutants are useful tools for studying the mechanisms of synapse assembly and catalysis.
synapsis is an important part of the reaction mechanism, and it can be used to control the reaction rate.
the synapse for resolvase is formed by sequential binding of dimers to the two sites, and that cleavage is slow relative to synapsis.
